extraFacts.fact: Wound fin tube listings: L-foot 120-150 C typical maker limit, KL 260 C typical, LL 155 C typical.
KL knurled wound fin tube listed sizes: 19.05, 25.4 and 38.1 mm base tube, 44.45, 57.15 and 69.85 mm fin OD.

faqs.q: What are crimped fin tubes used for?
faqs.a: The Crimped Fin Tubes have fin strip crimped (ruffled) at its root as it is wound onto the base tube, for economisers, air heaters and HVAC coils. Steel fins on steel tube are common in boiler economisers and air heaters, and copper and aluminium fins suit lower-temperature air and oil coolers.

faqs.q: What do I need to send to quote crimped fin tubes?
faqs.a: Send the base tube standard and grade, OD and wall, the fin type, material, height, thickness and fins per inch, the finned and bare lengths, overall length and quantity, the design temperature and gas, and any coating or galvanising. There is no fixed size table.

faqs.q: What sizes do the Crimped Fin Tubes come in?
faqs.a: Sizes are confirmed with the quotation: send the outside diameter, wall, length and quantity and we confirm what can be made. Finned tube is made to order on a finning line set up for each size.

faqs.q: How is a crimped fin formed on the tube?
faqs.a: The strip is fed edge-on to the tube and wound into a helix; as it bends, the inner edge gathers into small folds, the crimp, which gives the fin a wide, ruffled root that bears on the tube.

faqs.q: What temperature can the Crimped Fin Tubes take?
faqs.a: The listing gives no fixed temperature limit; copper and aluminium fins suit lower-temperature air and oil coolers, and steel fins suit hotter economisers and air heaters. State the design temperature and gas on the enquiry.

faqs.q: What materials are the Crimped Fin Tubes made from?
faqs.a: Base tube can be carbon steel, stainless steel, copper or copper alloy to the standard on the order, with carbon steel, stainless steel, copper or aluminium fins. Steel fin tubes are often hot-dip galvanised after finning to lock the fin to the tube.

faqs.q: Which certificates apply to the Crimped Fin Tubes?
faqs.a: Base tubes come with their mill certificates, fin bond and fin pitch are checked along the length, and a mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 is available on request. Third-party inspection can be arranged against your inspection and test plan.

faqs.q: What do crimped fin tubes fit into?
faqs.a: They go into boiler economisers, air heaters and HVAC coils; to replace existing tubes send the old drawing or a sample length so the new tubes fit the bundle and tube supports. See the [wound fin tubes shelf](/c/wound-fin-tubes-l-ll-kl).

faqs.q: How are the Crimped Fin Tubes packed and checked?
faqs.a: Finished tubes are packed in crates with the bare ends protected, and the fin bond and fin pitch are checked along the length. [Our finned tube fouling and cleaning guide](/blog/finned-tube-fouling-cleaning) covers cleaning in service.

faqs.q: How do crimped fins differ from L-foot wound fins?
faqs.a: A crimped fin gathers at the root into a ruffled helix, while the [L-Foot Tension-Wound Fin Tubes](/p/l-foot-tension-wound-fin-tubes) has an L-shaped foot that sits on the tube surface. Crimped fins suit economisers and air heaters, where L-foot fins suit air coolers.

faqs.q: Can you export the Crimped Fin Tubes from Dubai?
faqs.a: Yes. We ship Crimped Fin Tubes from Dubai, UAE to buyers across the GCC, Africa, Asia and beyond. Tubes ship crated with bare ends protected. Give the destination and quantity on [our contact page](/contact) and we quote the freight lane with the goods.

faqs.q: Do you keep the Crimped Fin Tubes in stock in Dubai?
faqs.a: Crimped Fin Tubes is quoted from Dubai, UAE against your drawing or data sheet rather than held as a standard item. Finned tube is made on a finning line set up for each size. Send the details through [our contact page](/contact) and we confirm the lead time with the quotation.

faqs.q: What are KL knurled wound fin tubes used for?
faqs.a: The KL Knurled Wound Fin Tubes are L-foot aluminium or copper fins tension-wound onto a base tube that is knurled first, so the foot is pressed into the knurl. They serve air-cooled exchanger services between the L-fin and embedded-fin temperatures.

faqs.q: How are the part numbers such as IH-TF-WF-KL-0190 read?
faqs.a: IH-TF-WF-KL-0190 is the 19.05 mm (3/4 in) base tube with a 44.45 mm fin OD and 12.7 mm fin height; IH-TF-WF-KL-0254 is 25.4 mm (1 in) tube with 57.15 mm fin OD, and IH-TF-WF-KL-0381 is 38.1 mm (1 1/2 in) tube with 69.85 mm fin OD.

faqs.q: What sizes do the KL Knurled Wound Fin Tubes come in?
faqs.a: The size table lists 3 sizes: 19.05, 25.4 and 38.1 mm base tube OD, wall 1.65–3.0 mm, 6–12 fins per inch and a 0.41 mm fin thickness, up to 18 m long. Other sizes are made on request.

faqs.q: What fin height and thickness do KL fins have?
faqs.a: The listing gives fin heights of 6–50 mm (common 9.5–16 mm) and thickness 0.3–0.5 mm, with the three listed sizes at 12.7 or 15.88 mm height. The base tube OD runs 15.88–165 mm, common 5/8 to 1 1/2 in.

faqs.q: What is the maximum service temperature of the KL Knurled Wound Fin Tubes?
faqs.a: The listing gives 260 °C as a typical maker limit, with published figures from 165 to 260 °C; confirm it with the maker for your order. The knurl gives a firmer bond than a plain L-foot, so KL fins hold at higher temperatures.

faqs.q: What materials are the KL Knurled Wound Fin Tubes made from?
faqs.a: Tube is carbon steel A179/A192/A106 B, stainless TP304/316/321 or copper alloy B111, and the fin is aluminium 1050/1060 or copper. State the base tube grade and fin material on the enquiry.

faqs.q: Which standards and certificates apply to the KL Knurled Wound Fin Tubes?
faqs.a: The KL Knurled Wound Fin Tubes are listed to API 661 / ISO 13706. The base tube is tested to its own specification, and a mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 is available on request.

faqs.q: What do the KL Knurled Wound Fin Tubes fit into?
faqs.a: They go into air-cooled exchanger bundles; for other finning methods see [HF welded spiral fin tubes](/c/hf-welded-spiral-fin-tubes), [embedded G-fin tubes](/c/embedded-g-fin-tubes) and [extruded fin tubes](/c/extruded-fin-tubes), and [Our guide to finned tube types](/blog/types-of-finned-tubes) compares them.

faqs.q: How is the bond made on the KL Knurled Wound Fin Tubes?
faqs.a: The base tube is knurled first and the L-foot is pressed into the knurl while the fin is tension-wound. Base tube is tested per its specification.

faqs.q: How do KL fins differ from plain L and LL wound fins?
faqs.a: The knurl gives a firmer bond than a plain L-foot, which is why KL holds up to about 260 °C against 120–150 °C for the [L-Foot Tension-Wound Fin Tubes](/p/l-foot-tension-wound-fin-tubes); the [LL Overlapped Wound Fin Tubes](/p/ll-overlapped-wound-fin-tubes) instead overlaps the feet to cover the tube. Choose on the service temperature.

faqs.q: Can you export the KL Knurled Wound Fin Tubes from Dubai?
faqs.a: Yes. We ship KL Knurled Wound Fin Tubes from Dubai, UAE to buyers across the GCC, Africa, Asia and beyond. Mill certificates are available on request. Give the destination and quantity on [our contact page](/contact) and we quote the freight lane with the goods.

faqs.q: Do you keep the KL Knurled Wound Fin Tubes in stock in Dubai?
faqs.a: KL Knurled Wound Fin Tubes is quoted from Dubai, UAE against your drawing or data sheet rather than held as a standard item. Finned tube is made on a finning line set up for each size. Send the details through [our contact page](/contact) and we confirm the lead time with the quotation.

faqs.q: What are L-foot tension-wound fin tubes used for?
faqs.a: The L-Foot Tension-Wound Fin Tubes are aluminium or copper fin strip with an L-shaped foot, tension-wound onto the base tube so each foot sits on the tube surface. They are the most economical air-cooler fin for moderate temperatures, used on low-temperature air coolers, lube-oil and jacket-water coolers and HVAC heaters.

faqs.q: How are part numbers such as IH-TF-WF-L-0254-B read?
faqs.a: IH-TF-WF-L-0254 and IH-TF-WF-L-0254-B are both 25.4 mm (1 in) tube, with fin OD 50.8 mm and 12.7 mm fin height for the first and fin OD 57.15 mm and 15.88 mm fin height for the -B suffix. The other rows are the 15.88, 19.05 and 38.1 mm tubes.

faqs.q: What sizes do the L-Foot Tension-Wound Fin Tubes come in?
faqs.a: The table lists 5 sizes on 15.88, 19.05, 25.4 and 38.1 mm base tube, at 10 fins per inch and 0.38 mm fin thickness, up to 18 m long. The listing gives base tube OD of 15.88–38.1 mm and fin height of 9.5–15.9 mm.

faqs.q: How many fins per inch can L-foot fin tubes have?
faqs.a: Fin density runs 4–12 FPI (157–472 fins/m), and the listed rows are at 10 FPI. Fin thickness is typically 0.38 mm (0.015 in), range 0.38–0.51 mm.

faqs.q: What is the maximum service temperature of the L-Foot Tension-Wound Fin Tubes?
faqs.a: The listing gives 120 °C as a conservative limit and 120–150 °C as the typical maker limit, because the bond is contact pressure only and loosens with time and temperature cycling. Use KL or LL fins for higher temperatures.

faqs.q: What materials are the L-Foot Tension-Wound Fin Tubes made from?
faqs.a: Tube can be carbon steel, stainless or copper alloy, and fins are aluminium 1100-O, a 5xxx aluminium alloy or copper. State the base tube grade and fin material on the enquiry.

faqs.q: Which standards apply to the L-Foot Tension-Wound Fin Tubes?
faqs.a: The L-Foot Tension-Wound Fin Tubes are listed to API 661 / ISO 13706 and ASME SA210; no fin bond test standard was found, and the base tube is tested to its own specification. A mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 is available on request.

faqs.q: What do the L-Foot Tension-Wound Fin Tubes fit into?
faqs.a: They go into air-cooled exchanger and cooler bundles; API 661 calls for cast zinc bands at the tube ends to stop footed fins unwinding. See the [wound fin tubes shelf](/c/wound-fin-tubes-l-ll-kl) and [Our guide to finned tube types](/blog/types-of-finned-tubes) for other finning methods.

faqs.q: Why are the ends of L-foot fin tubes banded?
faqs.a: The bond is contact pressure only, so the ends are banded to stop the fins unwinding, and API 661 calls for cast zinc bands at the tube ends. The bond can loosen with temperature cycling.

faqs.q: How do L-foot fins differ from KL and LL wound fins?
faqs.a: A plain L-foot is the most economical, but the [KL Knurled Wound Fin Tubes](/p/kl-knurled-wound-fin-tubes) adds a knurl for a firmer bond up to about 260 °C, and the [LL Overlapped Wound Fin Tubes](/p/ll-overlapped-wound-fin-tubes) overlaps the feet for full tube cover in humid and coastal plants.

faqs.q: Can you export the L-Foot Tension-Wound Fin Tubes from Dubai?
faqs.a: Yes. We ship L-Foot Tension-Wound Fin Tubes from Dubai, UAE to buyers across the GCC, Africa, Asia and beyond. Mill certificates are available on request. Give the destination and quantity on [our contact page](/contact) and we quote the freight lane with the goods.

faqs.q: Do you keep the L-Foot Tension-Wound Fin Tubes in stock in Dubai?
faqs.a: L-Foot Tension-Wound Fin Tubes is quoted from Dubai, UAE against your drawing or data sheet rather than held as a standard item. Finned tube is made on a finning line set up for each size. Send the details through [our contact page](/contact) and we confirm the lead time with the quotation.

faqs.q: What are LL overlapped wound fin tubes used for?
faqs.a: The LL Overlapped Wound Fin Tubes are tension-wound L-foot fins whose feet overlap one another, so the base tube is covered completely. The full cover protects the tube from the atmosphere, which suits air coolers in humid and coastal plants.

faqs.q: How are part numbers such as IH-TF-WF-LL-0254-B read?
faqs.a: IH-TF-WF-LL-0254 and IH-TF-WF-LL-0254-B are both 25.4 mm (1 in) tube, with 50.8 mm fin OD at 12.7 mm fin height and 57.15 mm fin OD at 15.88 mm fin height respectively. IH-TF-WF-LL-0190 is the 19.05 mm tube and IH-TF-WF-LL-0381 the 38.1 mm tube.

faqs.q: What sizes do the LL Overlapped Wound Fin Tubes come in?
faqs.a: The size table lists 4 sizes on 19.05, 25.4 and 38.1 mm base tube, 6–12 fins per inch, fin thickness 0.41 mm and up to 18 m long. The listing gives base tube OD of 19–51 mm and fin height of 10–16 mm.

faqs.q: What fin materials and thickness do LL fins have?
faqs.a: Fins are aluminium or copper, 0.3–0.5 mm thick and 10–16 mm high. Tubes can be carbon steel, stainless TP316/316L or Cu-Ni.

faqs.q: What is the maximum service temperature of the LL Overlapped Wound Fin Tubes?
faqs.a: The listing gives 155 °C as a typical maker limit, published 155–180 °C. Confirm it for your duty with the quotation, since the bond is tension winding with overlapping feet.

faqs.q: What materials are the LL Overlapped Wound Fin Tubes made from?
faqs.a: Tube is carbon steel, stainless TP316/316L or Cu-Ni, and the fins are aluminium or copper. State the grades on the enquiry.

faqs.q: Which certificates apply to the LL Overlapped Wound Fin Tubes?
faqs.a: The listing names no product standard; the base tube is tested to its own specification, and a mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 is available on request with third-party inspection by arrangement.

faqs.q: What do the LL Overlapped Wound Fin Tubes fit into?
faqs.a: They are used in moderate-temperature air coolers; see [our guide to extruded fin tubes for coastal air coolers](/blog/extruded-fin-tubes-coastal-air-coolers) for extruded fins on coastal coolers, and the [wound fin tubes shelf](/c/wound-fin-tubes-l-ll-kl) for the rest of the range.

faqs.q: What should I do to keep wound fin tubes clean in service?
faqs.a: Dirt between fins cuts performance, and [our finned tube fouling and cleaning guide](/blog/finned-tube-fouling-cleaning) sets out cleaning routes for finned tubes. The overlapped foot gives high atmospheric corrosion resistance because the base tube is fully covered.

faqs.q: How do LL fins differ from plain L-foot fins?
faqs.a: The overlapped foot covers the tube completely, so atmospheric corrosion resistance is high, while the [L-Foot Tension-Wound Fin Tubes](/p/l-foot-tension-wound-fin-tubes) leaves the tube exposed between feet and is limited to 120–150 °C. LL holds up to about 155 °C.

faqs.a: LL Overlapped Wound Fin Tubes is quoted from Dubai, UAE against your drawing or data sheet rather than held as a standard item. Finned tube is made on a finning line set up for each size. Send the details through [our contact page](/contact) and we confirm the lead time with the quotation.

faqs.q: What are notched and root-serrated fin tubes used for?
faqs.a: The Notched and Root-Serrated Fin Tubes are wound fins notched or serrated at the root, so the strip bends round the tube without stretching, for air coolers and heat-recovery coils. A notched or serrated fin can do the same duty in a smaller coil than a plain wound fin.

faqs.q: What do I need to send to quote notched fin tubes?
faqs.a: Send the base tube standard and grade, OD and wall, the fin type, material, height, thickness and fins per inch, the finned and bare lengths, overall length and quantity, the design temperature and the gas or air, and any coating. There is no fixed size table.

faqs.q: What sizes do the Notched and Root-Serrated Fin Tubes come in?
faqs.a: Sizes are confirmed with the quotation: send the OD, wall, length and quantity and we confirm what can be made. They are made to order on a finning line set up for each size.

faqs.q: What does notching or serrating the fin do?
faqs.a: Notching the root lets the strip bend round the tube without thinning or tearing, and serrating the outer edge breaks the fin into segments. The segments restart the air boundary layer at each cut, which raises the air-side heat-transfer coefficient for a modest rise in pressure drop.

faqs.q: What pressure drop and heat-transfer gain can I expect from the Notched and Root-Serrated Fin Tubes?
faqs.a: Serrations raise the air-side heat-transfer coefficient for a modest rise in pressure drop; the listing gives no fixed figure. State your duty on the enquiry so the fin is selected for it.

faqs.q: What materials are the Notched and Root-Serrated Fin Tubes made from?
faqs.a: Base tube can be carbon steel, stainless steel, copper or copper alloy, with aluminium, copper or carbon steel fins. State the grades on the enquiry.

faqs.q: Which certificates apply to the Notched and Root-Serrated Fin Tubes?
faqs.a: Base tubes come with their mill certificates and the fin bond and fin pitch are checked along the length. A mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 is available on request, and third-party inspection can be arranged.

faqs.q: What do notched fin tubes fit into?
faqs.a: They go into air coolers, heat-recovery coils and air heaters; to replace existing tubes send the old drawing or a sample length. See the [wound fin tubes shelf](/c/wound-fin-tubes-l-ll-kl), [HF welded spiral fin tubes](/c/hf-welded-spiral-fin-tubes) and [Our guide to finned tube types](/blog/types-of-finned-tubes) for other fin types.

faqs.q: How are the Notched and Root-Serrated Fin Tubes packed and checked?
faqs.a: Finished tubes are packed in crates with the bare ends protected, and fin bond and pitch are checked along the length. [Our finned tube fouling and cleaning guide](/blog/finned-tube-fouling-cleaning) covers keeping them clean.

faqs.q: How do notched or serrated fins differ from plain wound fins?
faqs.a: A plain wound fin like the [L-Foot Tension-Wound Fin Tubes](/p/l-foot-tension-wound-fin-tubes) is a continuous strip, while a notched or serrated root-and-edge fin raises the air-side coefficient so the coil can be smaller. See [our serrated versus solid spiral fin tube guide](/blog/serrated-vs-solid-spiral-fin-tubes) for serrated versus solid spiral fins.
